description:
src/backend.rs:134-194: the default impl of query_subtree is gated on 'where Self: Sized' (line 142). This is fine — trait default impls with async-fn-in-trait often need Sized for the returned Future to size correctly. But:

1. The other methods on FileNodeBackend (create_object, update_object, etc.) do NOT have an explicit Self: Sized bound, suggesting the trait is meant to be both object-safe-eligible AND usable through generic parameters. query_subtree alone has it, which makes the trait *not* object-safe.

2. The trait-level doc at src/backend.rs:32-33 says 'This trait is not object-safe by design (generic methods). Use Arc<impl FileNodeBackend> when sharing across tasks.' So object-safety was already not a design goal. Good.

3. But the Self: Sized bound on the default impl is unexplained. A reader hitting it asks 'why this one?'. The likely answer: the closure inside the async block at line 148 captures self by reference and the future type needs to be Sized to box.

Required: add a one-line comment explaining the Self: Sized bound, OR remove it if the impl actually compiles without it. The unexplained bound is a paper-cut for readers studying the trait.
title: FileNodeBackend::query_subtree default impl uses 'Self: Sized' bound, blocks object-safe usage but is undocumented
